title: Physical stability in the dorsal stream
paper: Pramod, Cohen, Tenenbaum and Kanwisher 2022, eLife

steps.title: Define the regions first
steps.paper: A physics localizer, predicting where a block tower falls against judging its colours, defined frontoparietal regions in each person before the test.
steps.here: TRIBE has no task, so the regions are anatomical: the intraparietal sulcus and superior parietal gyrus.

steps.title: Unstable against stable
steps.paper: Frontoparietal regions responded more to unstable scenes than to stable ones.
steps.here: The same fall, ending on the counter or stopping in mid-air with nothing holding it.

steps.title: The ventral pathway
steps.paper: The ventral visual pathway held no stability information that generalised across scenarios.
steps.here: The same contrast read in the fusiform gyrus.

steps.title: Change the outcome live
steps.paper: Stability is the only thing that differs between conditions.
steps.here: The agent sets the outcome control; Isaac renders the fall and TRIBE reads it.

steps.title: Match the motion
steps.paper: Low-level differences were tested across scenarios and against image-trained networks.
steps.here: The landing clip keeps bouncing while the hover is still. The control hovers with the same bounces, so only support differs.

args.title: Falling objects that bounce on air

bindings.event: a falling object bounces on air

steps.title: Across items
steps.paper: The stability signal generalised across scenario types.
steps.here: Each item is one scenario. The table sorts items by the effect in the intraparietal sulcus.
